findings: The current 17–30 passage has a complete death ending, but M29 opens with an empty tomb without an intervening burial. Existing HS-CF-06 correctly identifies 19:38–42 as required source context.

John19:31–37, also omitted, gives the soldiers' actions, Jesus already dead, the side pierced, and the eyewitness testimony/Scripture fulfillment. Those verses form the narrative and evidentiary sequence between death and burial; adding only vv38–42 would still skip the stated confirmation of death.

Restore the continuous John19:17–42. This retains Jesus' final saying/prayer, the death, witness to the death, and burial under Joseph and Nicodemus; keep the next movement's Johannine empty-tomb passage distinct.
safeOmissions: No verses inside John19:17–42 are judged safe to omit from the Calvary-to-burial sequence. Synoptic Passion accounts remain separate.
v7Evidence: The P3 desk pass reports CPDV and Douay verse presence for John19:38–42. V7 source selections contain the Johannine death/burial passage family; this confirms that burial has source support, not authorization to change the Bible text.

findings: The proof skips 20:4–5, losing the beloved disciple's race to the tomb and initial look inside. The following v8 calls him 'the other disciple' and says he had arrived first; the reason for that status is omitted.
It skips v10, so Mary's return to the tomb (v11) follows the disciples' recognition (vv8–9) without the text stating they went back home. Restore both gaps.

John20:19 opens late on the same day and gives Jesus' appearance, mission, Spirit, and forgiveness authority; v24 explains Thomas was absent, vv25–29 stage his return and confession. That is a distinct later appearance, but the source unit itself is complete and carries its doctrinal culmination. Together the present A units support a continuous John20:1–29 reading; no need to stitch Matthew/Luke/Mark appearance details into it.
safeOmissions: Luke24:13–35 (H65-03 B) Emmaus is a separate resurrection appearance; safe as a compulsory scene omission only if Scripture remains available as a parallel companion. The existing reader should not imply John20 exhausts all appearances.
v7Evidence: V7 has multiple publisher references to John20 and Resurrection sources; where source references encompass a wider Gospel appearance sequence, that is not verse equivalence for the Johannine first-day events. No evidence in the existing row matrix warrants harmonizing Luke24 with John20.

findings: Acts1:6 begins 'those assembled together questioned him' and asks when Jesus will restore Israel. The selected text has no antecedent for the assembled group or for the risen Jesus' presence.

CF-07's 1:3–5 supplies appearances over forty days and the command to remain for the Father's promise, but v3 itself opens with 'to whom he also presented himself alive' whose referent is established by Acts1:1–2. Retain Acts1:1–5, then the existing 6–12 uninterrupted. Verses 9–12 provide a complete Ascension scene, the angelic answer and return to Jerusalem.

This preserves the explicit Spirit promise that sets up Pentecost without implying that Luke's Gospel ending and Acts1 have been blended. No separate calendar date or exact Ascension location beyond the text's Mount of Olives is inferred.
safeOmissions: Do not add an external chronology or forty-day schedule beyond Acts1:3. The rest of Acts1:1–12 is directly within the selected introduction and Ascension.
v7Evidence: P3's bridge manifest independently verifies Acts1:3–5 verse presence in both installed Catholic witnesses. The extension to 1:1–2 follows the local syntax and book opening; it is a local textual-continuity correction, not an Atlas event addition.

movements.decision: RESTORE FULL PENTECOST SPEECH AND COMPLETE STEPHEN SCENE
findings: Acts2:11 begins 'likewise' and depends on the nationalities in vv9–10. Restore 9–10. The chosen v16–18 Joel quotation omits vv19–20, then v21 is its conclusion; retain vv19–21.

The proof jumps from the quote's closing v21 to the crowd's response in v37, omitting Peter's proclamation of Jesus' deeds, death, Resurrection and exaltation and scriptural argument (vv22–36). 'When they had heard these things' in v37 has no speech antecedent otherwise. Restore vv22–36; the full Pentecost-to-community source sequence is Acts2:1–47, including H68-01's continuous community description.

Stephen's selected text starts at 7:54 with 'upon hearing these things' but omits Stephen's identity/trial, the high priest's question, and Stephen's full speech. CF-08's 7:51–53 is only the speech's final accusation; it is not enough to identify its speaker or supply the argument. Since H68-04 is classified A, preserve the full independent pericope Acts6:8–7:60, including Stephen's introduction and complete speech, and its two prayers at vv59–60. This is long, but the speech and prayer are not safely compressible by target length.
safeOmissions: Acts3–6 before Stephen are an explicit timeline compression; retain a visible editorial ellipsis but do not invent a continuous next-day sequence. Acts3:1–10 and Acts8:26–40 remain separate C stories.
v7Evidence: V7 Pentecost related scope is Acts2:1–41 in publisher rows; the existing source matrix supports the chapter-scale account, not the current broken selection. Stephen is a separate Acts7 narrative, so no source record justifies jumping into its response without its hearing/speech.

movements.decision: RESTORE THE TWO FOUNDATIONAL NARRATIVES CONTINUOUSLY
findings: Acts9:17 follows Saul's blindness directly with Ananias entering, but vv12–16 (Saul's vision of Ananias, Ananias' objection, the Lord's choice of Saul and foretold suffering) are omitted. Restore 12–16 to keep call, mission and cost in the text; do not shorten the conversion dialogue.

Acts10:19 starts in the middle of Peter's vision aftermath; 24 skips the messengers' arrival, 28–29 skips Cornelius' reception, and 33 skips Cornelius' account of the angel's instruction. The whole 1–48 episode forms the causal chain: Cornelius' vision → Peter's vision → Spirit's direction → meeting and explanation → Peter's Gospel proclamation → Spirit upon Gentiles → baptism. Restore Acts10:1–48 whole.
Acts11:1–18 is the same Cornelius event retold by Peter to Jerusalem and classified D. It can remain unfeatured; do not make it a second event in the timeline.
safeOmissions: No verse within Acts10:1–48 is safe to omit for this decisive Gentile-inclusion event. Later mission episodes need not be added here.
v7Evidence: The P1 evidence records Cornelius as one event and treats repeated Acts11 narration as the same episode; the V7 master confirms publisher references as citation evidence only. It provides no justification for splitting the visions, explanation or Spirit arrival.

movements.decision: RESTORE MISSION RETURN AND COMPLETE COUNCIL PROCEEDINGS
findings: Acts13:1–5 completes the dispatch scene at Antioch; its full v18 unit continues to 12 with Cyprus events, but those are a separate mission episode, not needed to make the sending itself intelligible. The current review records that omission as safe if the chapter is presented as dispatch, not completed journey.

Before the Council, Acts14:26–28 (H71-03 B, source 14:19–28) is the shortest source-authentic return report: Paul and Barnabas report what God did and how the door of faith was opened to Gentiles. Add 14:26–28 to supply the mission's result and the issue's basis without adding each separate town.

At the Council, proof skips 15:3–4, which says Paul/Barnabas report the Gentile conversion and are received by the Church; restore. It skips v12, where the assembly hears Barnabas/Paul's signs, then v13 has James respond after silence; restore v12. Better retain 15:1–29 continuously so Peter's case, mission testimony, James' judgment, decision and letter remain in order.
safeOmissions: Acts12 and individual missionary scenes from Acts13–14 are not required if the return report 14:26–28 is retained and the ellipsis is visible. The Acts15 speeches are not safe to abridge for length.
v7Evidence: Existing source evidence differentiates the Antioch mission commissioning, Gentile conversion and Council event; the Council's selected 15:1–29 range is also found as a complete publisher pericope in independent source families. No V7 selection makes one mission stop equivalent to the full Council.

movements.decision: RESTORE ROME INTENTION, ARRIVAL AND THE COMPLETE LOCAL HEARING
findings: Acts28:23 begins after a prior appointed meeting; without 17–22 the reader does not know Paul's arrival, the local Jewish leaders' visit, the Roman imprisonment context or their invitation to hear his teaching. Restore Acts28:16–22; the smallest full local unit is Acts28:16–31.

Acts19:21 records Paul's expressed intention to go to Rome, and 28:16 records actual arrival. Retain them as separately dated-in-text itinerary hinges, not a direct same-scene transition; the intervening journey, arrest and voyage are compressed. The shipwreck is an independent C unit and need not be read to establish the Rome ending.
Acts28:23–31 itself remains the complete final proclamation and open ending; keep both statements to Jews and Gentiles (vv23–28), then the two-year preaching summary (vv30–31).
safeOmissions: Acts16/17/18/20 individual missionary episodes and Acts27 shipwreck remain independent stories; their omission is safe only with an explicit chronological ellipsis between Acts19:21 and 28:16.
v7Evidence: P3 bridge manifest verifies Acts19:21 and 28:16 verse coordinates in CPDV and Douay. The source matrix has no evidence to collapse the intervening itinerary into a one-stop trip. The new boundary adds source text around the already selected Acts28:23–31.

findings: Revelation5:1 begins with a scroll in the hand of 'the one seated upon the throne', which the selected text has not introduced. The adjacent source unit Revelation4:1–11 supplies John's entry into the vision, the throne, the one seated, and heavenly worship. Add it; 4:1–5:14 is a coherent two-chapter throne/Lamb vision.

Revelation1:9–20 locates the seer and introduces Christ among the lampstands, while chapters2–3 are distinct messages. For the strictly focused throne-room scene, omitting those preceding messages is a marked vision-cycle ellipsis, not a missing cause inside ch4–5. Cite the opening vision as companion if the public sequence otherwise starts without introducing John.
Do not stage the slain Lamb's scroll as a date-stamped event following Paul's Rome journey; this remains apocalyptic vision. Preserve every verse of 4 and 5.
safeOmissions: Individual letters in Rev2–3, and H74-01 (1:9–20), are not part of the immediate throne-room cause-and-response sequence if M35 begins as a separate vision selection with a clear Scripture source label.
v7Evidence: Existing V7 has a specific Lamb/scroll source selection at Revelation5:1–14 as source scope. The local textual antecedent for its throne is Revelation4, already classified B. Keep those existing unit identifiers; do not create a new Atlas event.

movements.decision: RESTORE LAMB'S WEDDING/JUDGMENT PRELUDE; KEEP VISION GENRE
findings: Rev19:11 starts 'after these things' and enters the opened heaven/horseman scene. Rev19:1–10 is the immediately preceding heavenly praise, judgment of Babylon and marriage of the Lamb; include it to preserve the vision's stated sequence and bride context.

Rev20:1–15 is already continuous and carries the binding, reign, final release/defeat and great-white-throne judgment. Keep all 15 verses; the sequence contains theological material that cannot be trimmed without changing the vision's stages.

Rev12:1–17 (B) presents a symbolic conflict from another vision cycle. Since Revelation uses recapitulating imagery and the desk pass forbids a simple literal historical chronology, retain it as a separately cited context link, not a missing linear episode to be spliced before Rev19.
safeOmissions: The selected final sequence need not import Rev6–18 as a dated travelogue or merge the dragon/beast cycles into one literal event sequence. Keep source references to them available through existing Scripture navigation.
v7Evidence: The V7 master classifies Revelation sources as printed references and does not validate a chronological harmonization. The present expansion 19:1–10 is internal local context for the existing 19:11 pericope; no new geographical claim follows.

movements.decision: RESTORE COMPLETE NEW-JERUSALEM VISION AND APOCALYPSE EPILOGUE
findings: Current source jumps from 21:1–7 to 22:1–5, dropping 21:8–27: the contrast with exclusion, angel's measuring of the city, gates/foundations, nations and Lamb's light. This is not a safe gap within the New Creation vision. Keep 21:1–22:5 uninterrupted.

The current endpoint at 22:5 closes the vision image but leaves Revelation's final testimony and invitation (22:6–21) unread. Since this is the concluding movement of the whole sequence, include the epilogue, including the promise of Christ's coming, the Spirit/bride's invitation and final warning/blessing. Retain all text and genre distinctions; do not turn its timing language into a dated geography scene.

The P3 12-hazard register appropriately warns against a simple chronological staging of apocalyptic visions. The full conclusion is a canonical endpoint, not a claim that every symbolic image is a time-stamped event.
safeOmissions: No verse within the actual New Creation and epilogue ending (Rev21:1–22:21) is classified safe to omit for a complete final reading. The preceding visionary cycles remain outside this movement with an explicit boundary.
v7Evidence: V7's Revelation references are evidence of selected printed spans, not a license to treat the Apocalypse as a literal itinerary. The P3 status already treats Rev21–22 as final canonical boundary; this review restores omitted verses inside it.

guards: Original 217-unit source classifications retained; additions are source candidates only.
Scripture wording, canonical Atlas IDs and reader are unmodified.
Visionary texts are not converted to a literal continuous chronology.
